findings.title: A curtain the watchdog mounts before the fonts arrive never gets its observers: no tray-fold turn, recuts only through the drift watch
findings.where: scripts/glass.mjs:3810-3811 (refreshGlass's mount waits for document.fonts.ready, then mount() and observe() only when no curtain stands); glass.mjs:3842-3846 (the 4 s and 9 s watchdog calls mount() alone)
findings.what_happens: registerGlass calls refreshGlass, which defers the mount to document.fonts.ready. If the fonts are not in by 4000 ms, the watchdog finds no curtain and calls mount(), which pushes the curtain and starts the loop but connects no observer. When the fonts then arrive, go() sees curtains.length > 0 and skips both mount() and observe(). observe() is called nowhere else, so that page has no MutationObserver on Foundry's columns, no ResizeObserver on the blocks or the rails and no watchTrayFold for the session; only the drift watch (two samples 500 ms apart) and the resize listener recut it.
findings.failure_scenario: A player on a slow connection whose Stained Glass faces take over four seconds to load folds the Projects tray all evening and the glass jumps to the new cut a second later instead of turning with it, and a block that appears is recut a second late.
findings.expected: Whatever mounts the curtain also observes it (the watchdog calls observe() after mount(), or mount() does).
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for another caller of observe(): grep finds only 3810. Looked for a later refreshGlass that would observe: with a curtain up refreshGlass goes to rebuild() (3804), never to go(). R1420 covers a theme switched before the fonts arrive, not the watchdog's mount. Whether fonts.ready takes over 4 s at a real table is not measured (not_established).

findings.title: Two exported convexOverlap functions with different answers, and two centroid helpers with different definitions, in the same family
findings.where: scripts/glass.mjs:2708-2723 (convexOverlap: the overlap polygon or null); scripts/glass-close.mjs:54-59 (convexOverlap: a boolean, the separating-axis test); glass-geometry.mjs:1258 (centroid: the bounding box's middle) against glass-close.mjs:30 (centroid: the mean of the corners, glass-geometry's meanOf)
findings.what_happens: glass.mjs uses its own convexOverlap to clip the frost (3006) and treats the answer as a polygon; glass-close.mjs's is a test ('a shared edge is not an overlap', a copy of glass-geometry's overlaps). The names collide across files that read each other's names (glass.mjs imports from glass-close.mjs), so an import changed to the other file's convexOverlap would turn a polygon into true. centroid has the same split: the turn's matching (turnPlan 2555-2558) uses the box middle, the fill's slides (slidePlan) the corners' mean.
findings.failure_scenario: A later stage moving the frost's clip into glass-close.mjs imports convexOverlap from there, the frost is clipped to path('M...true') and the panes that stand lose their blur on every fold of the tray.
findings.expected: One name per meaning (overlapPolygon / overlapsConvex), and one centroid.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that today's callers each use their own file's: glass.mjs 3006 its own, glass-close.mjs 133 and 388 its own; no wrong import today, so this is a trap, not a fault.
